title: Путёвка от Елены Павловны  (A Vacation Voucher from Elena Pavlovna)

segments.t: Outside the hospital, Elena Pavlovna reminds Chef Barinov that his doctor strictly forbade any kitchen work during his recovery. To make sure he actually rests, she surprises him with a vacation voucher for a flight departing in just four hours.
Надо как-то заскочить к вам в ресторан, посмотреть.
Ну, а что вы так реагируете.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.

'No work whatsoever, do you understand?' Barinov asks whether work whatsoever do Vika understands, refusing to let the point slide. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'Yes, yes, no work at all.' Telling Barinov to work at all moves the conversation forward without extra drama.
'Do you understand? Yes?' By asking whether Vika understands, Barinov presses Vika for a straight answer.
Надо как-то заскочить к вам в ресторан, посмотреть.

'I should drop by your restaurant sometime to take a look.' Noting that she should drop by Barinov's restaurant sometime to take a look keeps Vika's side of the story simple and clear. There is no "you" needed in the Russian here: one short word states the rule for everyone in the room.

'Where are you rushing off to like that?' Asking where Vika rushing off to like is is how Barinov puts Vika on the spot. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'If you also stop by to have a meal.' Admitting that if Barinov also stop by to have a meal shows Vika being honest for a change.
'Viktor Petrovich.' With the hospital and work in play, Barinov keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'Your plane leaves in four hours.' Once Barinov's plane leaves in four hours, Vika can finally tell Barinov what she means.
Ну, а что вы так реагируете.
'Well, why are you reacting like that.' Adding that why are Vika reacting like fills in the missing piece for Vika.
'Wait, right now?' Turning from the doctor to the point, Vika asks Barinov directly. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.

'Right this minute? Well?' Around the doctor and plan, Barinov wants to know where Vika really stands. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Well, no.' Between the hospital and the moment, Vika gives Barinov a quick, grounded response.
'I am ready.' Adding that he is ready fills in the missing piece for Vika. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
Надо как-то заскочить к вам в ресторан, посмотреть.
Ну, а что вы так реагируете.

That wraps up this scene as as Chef Barinov leaves the hospital under strict orders not to work, Elena Pavlovna surprises him with a last-minute vacation flight leaving in four hours. See you next time!
